comments.author: @giannisolga5191
comments.text: I have a friend from Rhodesia who in the past worked as an anaesthetist in Orangemund. He told me about the workers having to get x-rayed to see if they had swallowed any diamonds. A couple of chilling things I've learned about the Nazis are firstly Hitler said before he came to power "Who thinks today about the Armenian genocide?" So the idea of a genocide was going through his mind before he had the power and means to order genocide. But the second thing which gave me a chill was this. In Windhoek there is a Hermann Göring Street. So I thought, OK they named it after Hitler's Marshal of the Luftwaffe during the Nazi period.  Nope. The name goes further back. It's named for Hermann Göring, Sr. - Göring's father. So Göring had a father who'd been part of the Herero genocide. So genocide was a thing, and not a tabu. I've been on a ship en route from Southampton to Cape Town. There's a sort of background noise the whole time underway. But when we passed the Skeleton Coast everything became quiet. My theory is that the massive sand dunes absorb the sounds from the ocean. And one could feel that the air was suddenly extremely dry. Stays quite clearly in my memory. thank you for the amazing insights. A beetle that stands on its head to collect the dew waterl Beautiful Etosha. Traveling with you is so rewarding!

comments.author: @deirdrelewis1454
comments.text: I’m South African. I live in Cape Town. I’ve visited Namibia twice. It’s a harsh but beautiful land, still mainly underdeveloped. One of my nursing colleagues came from the spergebiet. She told me about a beach totally covered in garnets. I also worked with a doctor who inherited a private diamond mine from his German grandfather. It’s a fascinating country to visit.
